Review the conversation context below and respond with a concise summary
of important items that should be preserved in the daily log.
Do NOT use any tools — just return plain text.

Format your response as a structured daily log entry with these sections:

**Context:** [One line about what the user was working on]

**Key Exchanges:**
- [Important Q&A or discussions]

**Decisions Made:**
- [Any decisions with rationale]

**Lessons Learned:**
- [Gotchas, patterns, or insights discovered]

**Action Items:**
- [Follow-ups or TODOs mentioned]

Skip anything that is:
- Routine tool calls or file reads
- Content that's trivial or obvious
- Trivial back-and-forth or clarification exchanges

Only include sections that have actual content. If nothing is worth saving,
respond with exactly: FLUSH_OK

## Conversation Context

**Assistant:** I am finding the newest handoff. The newest one is `docs/handoffs/2026-10-23-audit-followup.md`. Now I check its open items.

**Assistant:** I am checking the open items from the newest sessions. Most are already done. I am looking at the last few.

**Assistant:** Flush test passes. Now I close the old KeystoneOS item.

**Assistant:** Now the memory lint report. I compare yesterday's findings with today's.

**Assistant:** I am finding the program that makes the lint report. Then I see why it flags old, fixed items again.

**Assistant:** Now I fix the lint program in three small places.

**Assistant:** Now I fix the lint program in three small places.

**Assistant:** I keep a copy of the weekly report. Then I run the lint again to test the fix (about 3 minutes).

**Assistant:** Lint went from 1 error + 37 warnings to 0 errors + 15 warnings. Now I read the 12 that are left.

**Assistant:** Twelve real stale notes are left. They are small. I fix them in place, the same way the 10-24 session did ("Superseded" marks, nothing deleted).

**Assistant:** Notes are fixed. I fix one index hint for Box, then run the fast lint check.

**Assistant:** Lint is clean: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Now I commit.

**Assistant:** Pushed. Last step: I update the handoff and `STATUS.md`.

**Assistant:** The new test passes, and it fails on the old code (good). Now I fix two more stale notes the lint missed.

**Assistant:** I picked up the newest handoff: `docs/handoffs/2026-10-23-audit-followup.md`. All of its open items are now closed, and the weekly memory check is clean.

**What I checked (all OK):**
- The cloud copy to Drive ran OK on 10-24 and 10-25.
- The weekly memory job ran at 02:30 last night. The error log is empty.
- The fix for the 10-21 flush error was already in place. Its test passes.
- The old KeystoneOS item ("confirm the memory index") is closed. Today's backup indexed the memory with no error.

**What I fixed:**
- The weekly memory check reported 1 error and 37 warnings. Most were not real. It kept flagging old facts that the 10-24 session had already marked "Superseded." It also flagged the short summary in `USER.md` for repeating facts from other files, which it is meant to do.
- I changed the check to skip those two cases. It also no longer counts an empty memory folder as an error.
- When I ran it again: 0 errors, 15 warnings. Then I fixed the 14 warnings that were real (out-of-date facts). I marked each one "Superseded" in place and deleted nothing.
- The quick structural check now shows 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- I added one small test for the empty-folder fix. It passes, and it fails on the old code.
- Everything is committed and pushed in four repos. `docs/STATUS.md` is updated.

**What you do now:** nothing is needed.

**One optional choice:** the daily backup skips its `uv` cache cleanup every day. The cache is locked while Claude sessions run. I recommend we log this as normal (INFO), not as a problem. I did not build this.

**What I did not check, and the risks:**
- I ran the full memory check only once after the fix. The full check uses a model, so its results can change from run to run.
- The check now trusts "Superseded" marks. If a current fact gets that mark by mistake, the check will not report it.
- `/usr/local/bin` is not empty. It holds `code` (the VS Code command). Your `machine.md` says it is empty. I did not change `machine.md`.
- Box Drive is not installed on the Mac. You need it only if a Box task comes up.

**User:** Eat with the optional step

**User:** Eat with the optional step

**Assistant:** I am making the `uv` cleanup skip a normal (INFO) log line.

**Assistant:** The skip is already not counted as an error. So the only change is the log text: it should say this is normal. Then nobody chases it again.

**Assistant:** Done. I read "Eat" as "Go" and did the optional step.

**What I changed:** when the daily backup cannot clean the `uv` cache because it is locked, the log now says that is normal:
`uv-prune: skipped (locked by a live uvx server; normal, retries next run)`

The backup already did not count this as an error. Only the wording changed, so nobody chases it again.

**Did it work?** Yes. The backup's offline test shows ALL PASS. The change is committed and pushed (dotclaude `68035d2`). `docs/STATUS.md` is pushed too. Another session had pushed to DEV first, so I pulled its changes in before I pushed. There was no conflict.

**What this costs you:** the `uv` cache is 24.9 GB. It gets cleaned only when no browser-use server is running. That has not happened yet, so the cache keeps growing. This is only disk space.

**What you do now:** nothing.

content.text:
**Context:** Picked up handoff `docs/handoffs/2026-10-23-audit-followup.md`, closed all its open items, and fixed false positives in the weekly memory lint.

**Key Exchanges:**
- Verified everything was healthy:
  - Drive cloud copy ran OK on 10-24 and 10-25.
  - The weekly memory job ran at 02:30 with an empty error log.
  - The fix for the 10-21 flush error was already in place, and its test passes.
- Closed the old KeystoneOS item ("confirm the memory index"). Today's backup indexed memory with no error.
- Weekly memory lint reported 1 error + 37 warnings, mostly false positives:
  - It re-flagged facts already marked "Superseded" by the 10-24 session.
  - It flagged the intentional summary in `USER.md` as duplication.
  - It counted an empty memory folder as an error.
- User replied "Eat with the optional step" (read as "Go"), approving the `uv` log wording change.

**Decisions Made:**
- Lint now skips "Superseded"-marked facts and the `USER.md` summary, and no longer treats an empty memory folder as an error.
  - Result: 0 errors, 15 warnings.
  - Fixed the 14 real stale notes by marking them "Superseded" in place, deleting nothing. This follows the 10-24 convention.
  - The structural lint is now 0/0.
- Added a regression test for the empty-folder fix. It passes on the new code and fails on the old.
- Committed and pushed across four repos, and updated `docs/STATUS.md`.
- The daily backup's `uv` cache prune skip is now logged as normal INFO: `uv-prune: skipped (locked by a live uvx server; normal, retries next run)`.
  - It was already not counted as an error. Only the wording changed, so nobody chases it again.
  - Committed as dotclaude `68035d2`. Backup offline test shows ALL PASS.

**Lessons Learned:**
- The full memory lint uses a model, so results can vary between runs. It was only run once after the fix.
- Lint now trusts "Superseded" marks. A current fact marked superseded by mistake will no longer be caught.
- Another session had pushed to DEV first. Pulling before pushing avoided a conflict.
- The `uv` cache is locked whenever a browser-use uvx server is running, so pruning rarely happens.

**Action Items:**
- `uv` cache is 24.9 GB and growing because prune keeps getting skipped. Consider manual cleanup when no uvx servers are running.
- `machine.md` is out of date: it says `/usr/local/bin` is empty, but it holds `code` (the VS Code CLI). Not yet corrected.
- Box Drive is not installed on the Mac. Install it only if a Box task comes up.
- Optionally re-run the full memory lint to confirm stable results.
